phases.name: Pin the brief, latency clock, and operating assumptions
phases.description: Keep the supplied multimodal, conversational scope and hard targets distinct from unresolved product choices; agree how latency and answer accuracy will be measured before claiming either target is met.

phases.name: Connect channels and normalize text, image, and speech
phases.description: Use the real web and mobile palette entries, an explicitly generic adapter for additional channels, a shared API boundary, and the existing custom-component type for Azure Bot Service.

phases.name: Understand each turn and enrich it with language signals
phases.description: Normalize non-text inputs, orchestrate the turn, extract locale, intent, and entities, and add sentiment as a signal without letting it replace the user's intent.

phases.name: Ground answers, preserve conversation context, and plan scale
phases.description: Keep FAQ content distinct from its search index, return grounded results to the orchestrator, and retain only the state needed to continue a multi-turn conversation.

phases.name: Measure quality, observe conversations, and recover safely
phases.description: Instrument the complete turn, evaluate labeled outcomes against the strict accuracy target, scale from measured saturation, and define safe fallback behavior for unsupported or low-confidence cases.

steps.phase: Pin the brief, latency clock, and operating assumptions
steps.title: Carry forward the supplied problem without rewriting it
steps.content: The supplied description calls for processing text, images, and speech; conversational AI; user-intent understanding; and answers from knowledge bases. The eight functional requirements and five constraints remain the acceptance contract. The hints name Bot Service, LUIS, QnA Maker, Text Analytics, Cognitive Search, and Application Insights; treat them as solution clues, not proof that a particular SKU, integration, or service lifecycle has been validated.

steps.phase: Pin the brief, latency clock, and operating assumptions
steps.title: Make design assumptions visible before drawing services
steps.content: Working assumptions, not supplied requirements: web, mobile, and at least one messaging/voice integration represent the unspecified channel mix; the application may call managed Azure AI endpoints behind replaceable adapters; Semantic Kernel is a draft orchestration choice; active-session persistence is enabled as a draft recovery choice; conversation state is separated from long-term transcript retention; and the knowledge owner supplies approved FAQ content. Confirm the required channels, supported-language list, identity model, data residency, retention/consent rules, and ownership of knowledge updates before production sizing.

steps.phase: Pin the brief, latency clock, and operating assumptions
steps.title: Keep the two-second response target intact while defining its clock
steps.content: The brief says response latency under two seconds but does not define the start/stop events, percentile, or whether a response means the first useful streamed content or a complete answer. Keep the stated target unchanged. Instrument end-to-end turn latency separately for text, image, and speech, and ask the product owner to approve the measurement boundary before declaring a pass; do not quietly substitute a time-to-first-token or an average.

decision.question: What exactly must finish in under two seconds for each supported input mode?
decision.chosen: Preserve under two seconds as the hard target, report complete-turn and first-useful-response timings by modality, and get the acceptance clock and percentile confirmed before sign-off.
decision.chosenReason: The architecture can expose the timing evidence now without weakening or silently redefining the supplied constraint.

alternatives.tradeoff: It hides tail delays and says nothing about image or speech requests.

alternatives.option: Treat first token as the response for every request
alternatives.tradeoff: A quick acknowledgement can conceal a slow or unusable final answer.

steps.phase: Pin the brief, latency clock, and operating assumptions
steps.title: Define what the strict accuracy rate counts
steps.content: The constraint is accuracy above 85%, but it does not define a labeled set, task mix, language aggregation, or whether correctness means intent/entity extraction, FAQ answer correctness, or both. A working evaluation should report these dimensions separately and include an approved end-to-end answer rubric. Keep the target strictly greater than 85%; do not claim success until the owner approves the denominator, labels, and aggregation rule.

decision.question: How should the application demonstrate accuracy above 85%?
decision.chosen: Measure labeled intent/entity outcomes and grounded-answer correctness separately, then report the agreed end-to-end metric and per-language breakdown against a versioned evaluation set.
decision.chosenReason: Separate measures reveal whether a poor answer came from language understanding, retrieval, or response composition instead of letting a single aggregate hide the failure mode.

alternatives.tradeoff: Feedback is sparse and self-selected, so it is not a stable accuracy denominator.

alternatives.option: Average all languages and tasks into one number
alternatives.tradeoff: A strong high-volume locale can hide an unsupported or inaccurate language.

steps.phase: Pin the brief, latency clock, and operating assumptions
steps.title: Do not turn concurrency into an invented request rate
steps.content: The supplied capacity target is 10k+ concurrent conversations, not a requests-per-second figure. Conversation arrival rate, turns per conversation, payload size, channel mix, and session duration are unknown. Use a representative load profile and hold at least the stated concurrency during a measured test; derive replica counts, cache capacity, and quotas from those observations rather than guessing them here.

steps.phase: Pin the brief, latency clock, and operating assumptions
steps.title: Choose replaceable service boundaries, not palette inventions
steps.content: The catalog has generic web, mobile, gateway, AI-orchestration, and cache components, but no exact Azure Bot Service, LUIS, QnA Maker, Cognitive Search, Text Analytics, or Application Insights palette entries. Use the existing generic custom type for those named Azure services and keep their technology explicit in supported properties. This preserves the service choice without inventing component types or pretending a generic engine selector supports Azure.

decision.question: How should Azure-specific services appear when the component palette has no exact entry?
decision.chosen: Use an existing component when its catalog properties genuinely fit; otherwise use custom-component and describe the Azure service in its supported technology and purpose fields.
decision.chosenReason: The diagram remains buildable with current palette types while retaining the actual service boundary and its intended role.

alternatives.option: Create an Azure-specific component type in this walkthrough
alternatives.tradeoff: The new type is unsupported by the current frontend catalog and may fail when applied.

alternatives.option: Label an unrelated built-in component as Azure Cognitive Search
alternatives.tradeoff: Its supported provider options would misrepresent what the canvas can configure.

steps.phase: Connect channels and normalize text, image, and speech
steps.title: Add the browser client
steps.content: Use the existing Web App palette type for the browser channel. It sends text or supported media references through the common API boundary; the client should not call language, sentiment, or knowledge services directly. The specific web framework and number of client instances are not stated, so neither is asserted as a capacity fact.

component.label: Web Conversation Client
component.description: Browser entry point for text and supported media turns

properties.purpose: Capture user turns and render the bot response; submit through the shared API boundary and preserve channel and locale metadata.

component.highlightReason: Web App is the exact existing catalog component for a browser-based client; only its supported componentName and purpose fields are used.

steps.phase: Connect channels and normalize text, image, and speech
steps.title: Add the native mobile client
steps.content: Use the existing Mobile App palette type for iOS/Android clients. Carry the same conversation identifier and locale contract as the web client so switching channels does not silently start a different dialog. Offline behavior, push notifications, and a particular mobile stack are not specified and remain product decisions.

component.label: iOS / Android Conversation Client
component.description: Native mobile channel using the shared conversation contract

properties.purpose: Send and receive turns through the shared API contract; retain the conversation identifier and selected locale across client navigation.

component.highlightReason: Mobile App is the catalog's iOS/Android client type; no unrequested stack or session-count property is asserted.

steps.phase: Connect channels and normalize text, image, and speech
steps.title: Add adapters for the remaining supported channels
steps.content: The brief requires multiple channels without enumerating them. Use the custom type for the Bot Service channel adapters and configure only the channels the product approves, such as a messaging connector or voice endpoint. Normalize channel identity, message IDs, locale, attachments, and delivery receipts at this boundary; do not claim every connector is enabled merely because the adapter exists.

component.label: Bot Service Channel Adapters
component.description: Approved messaging and voice connectors beyond web and mobile

properties.subtitle: Messaging + voice connectors
properties.purpose: Connect only the product-approved external channels to the bot; normalize message identifiers, locale, attachment references, and delivery events behind replaceable adapters.
properties.notes: The brief does not name channels. Confirm connector requirements, authentication, payload limits, and channel-specific response capabilities before enabling each integration.

component.highlightReason: The catalog has no exact Bot Service or channel-adapter entry; the supported generic custom-component represents the Azure-specific boundary.

steps.phase: Connect channels and normalize text, image, and speech
steps.title: Add one validated API entry point
steps.content: Use the catalog API Gateway for the shared browser/mobile API path. Validate payload size and schema, authenticate where the product requires identity, apply abuse controls, and propagate a trace/conversation ID. A rate limit must be calibrated from the channel mix and service quotas; 10k+ concurrent conversations does not itself specify requests per second.

component.label: Conversation API Gateway
component.description: TLS, validation, routing, and abuse controls for client requests

properties.purpose: Validate request envelopes and media references, authenticate according to the approved identity model, enforce calibrated throttling, and propagate correlation and conversation IDs.

component.highlightReason: API Gateway is an exact catalog component with supported validation, authentication, rate-limiting, TLS, and throttling properties.

steps.phase: Connect channels and normalize text, image, and speech
steps.title: Route browser turns through the common boundary
steps.content: Send web turns and media references through the gateway rather than exposing internal AI endpoints. The request carries channel, locale, conversation ID, and a trace ID so the two-second response target can be measured across the application path.

connection.label: Text / media reference + locale
connection.description: Browser requests enter through the validated API boundary with correlation metadata.

steps.phase: Connect channels and normalize text, image, and speech
steps.title: Route mobile turns through the same contract
steps.content: Use the same API contract for mobile. This avoids duplicating validation, authentication, latency telemetry, and conversation semantics in a client-specific backend.

connection.label: Mobile turn + conversation ID
connection.description: Native clients share the same validated request and response boundary.

steps.phase: Connect channels and normalize text, image, and speech
steps.title: Add the bot framework boundary
steps.content: The palette has no Azure Bot Service entry, so use its supported custom type. This boundary owns channel delivery, conversation-turn identity, dialog handoff, and channel-specific response adaptation; it delegates language understanding and knowledge retrieval rather than embedding every concern in one opaque handler.

component.label: Azure Bot Service — Conversation Boundary
component.description: Channel-aware turn handling and response delivery

properties.subtitle: Turn lifecycle + channel delivery
properties.purpose: Accept authenticated channel turns, correlate each conversation, delegate language and answer work, apply channel-safe response formatting, and return the final response through the originating channel.
properties.notes: Keep channel adapters and service-specific SDK calls behind this boundary so the application can replace a connector without rewriting domain behavior.

component.highlightReason: Bot Service has no exact palette type; this uses only the generic custom-component and its actual supported properties.

steps.phase: Connect channels and normalize text, image, and speech
steps.title: Hand validated client turns to the bot framework
steps.content: The gateway forwards a validated turn with its authenticated principal, channel, locale, and correlation IDs. The bot boundary owns the response lifecycle, while downstream services remain private implementation dependencies.

connection.label: Authenticated turn + trace context
connection.description: The gateway forwards a bounded, validated request to the Bot Service boundary.

steps.phase: Connect channels and normalize text, image, and speech
steps.title: Connect the approved external channels to the bot
steps.content: External channel adapters deliver normalized turn events to the same Bot Service boundary. A channel lacking a needed modality or response feature must expose that limitation rather than silently dropping content.

connection.label: Approved channel events
connection.description: Channel-specific events are normalized before entering shared conversation handling.

steps.phase: Connect channels and normalize text, image, and speech
steps.title: Choose channel adapters over channel-specific bot logic
steps.content: Keep one conversation contract and translate channel differences at the adapter edge. Add a channel-specific orchestration branch only when the channel cannot express the shared interaction model; keep authentication, locale, message identity, retries, and delivery status explicit in that adapter.

decision.question: Should each channel have a separate conversation implementation?
decision.chosen: Use channel adapters feeding one Bot Service conversation boundary, with narrowly scoped capability handling at the edge.
decision.chosenReason: A shared turn model keeps behavior and observability consistent while still allowing channel-specific payload mapping.

alternatives.option: Fork the bot workflow for every channel
alternatives.tradeoff: Behavior and fixes drift, and every new channel multiplies test and release paths.

alternatives.option: Force every channel into the same raw payload format
alternatives.tradeoff: Channel features and delivery semantics may be lost or misrepresented.

steps.phase: Understand each turn and enrich it with language signals
steps.title: Add multimodal input normalization
steps.content: The problem description includes images and speech as well as text. Use the custom type for the media-normalization boundary: validate media references, apply approved size/type controls, transcribe speech or extract the needed image text/features, and pass normalized content plus provenance onward. Do not put large uploads or slow preprocessing on an unmeasured path and then claim the two-second target is met.

component.label: Speech + Image Input Normalization
component.description: Transcription and image text/feature extraction before language processing

properties.subtitle: Text, speech, image inputs
properties.purpose: Validate media references and supported formats; transcribe speech and extract only the image content needed by the conversation; attach locale, confidence, and source modality to normalized text/features.
properties.technology: Replaceable Azure speech and vision endpoints
properties.notes: The brief supplies no file-size, format, retention, or per-modality latency budget. Confirm them and measure preprocessing separately and end to end.

component.highlightReason: The palette has no exact speech/vision service type; the generic custom-component represents this Azure-specific preprocessing boundary.

steps.phase: Understand each turn and enrich it with language signals
steps.title: Add the turn orchestration component
steps.content: Use the existing AI Orchestrator palette component to sequence locale detection, intent/entity extraction, knowledge retrieval, response policy, and channel-aware composition. Its supported Semantic Kernel framework option is a concrete implementation choice for this draft, not a requirement; the adapter boundary permits another supported framework or a custom implementation after review.

component.label: Conversation Turn Orchestrator
component.description: Coordinates language signals, grounded retrieval, and response policy

properties.purpose: Coordinate intent/entity and sentiment calls, route answerable questions to the approved FAQ/search path, apply confidence and fallback policy, and compose a channel-aware response with source references.
properties.steps: normalize -> locale and intent -> retrieve grounded answer -> response policy -> channel response

component.highlightReason: AI Orchestrator is an existing palette type; its framework and pipeline-step fields are supported and fit the turn-coordination role.

steps.phase: Understand each turn and enrich it with language signals
steps.title: Pass each bot turn to the orchestrator
steps.content: The Bot Service hands the correlated turn and active conversation context to the orchestrator. Keep channel delivery concerns in the bot boundary and decision logic in the orchestrator so response customization remains testable without a channel SDK.

connection.label: Turn + locale + conversation context
connection.description: A single correlated turn enters the shared language, retrieval, and response-policy flow.

steps.phase: Understand each turn and enrich it with language signals
steps.title: Send speech and image turns through preprocessing
steps.content: The Bot Service invokes media normalization only when the turn contains speech or image content; text-only turns should not pay unnecessary preprocessing cost. Enforce authorization and content-handling policy before a media reference reaches an AI endpoint.

connection.label: Speech / image payload reference
connection.description: Only non-text or media-bearing turns invoke modality-specific normalization.

steps.phase: Understand each turn and enrich it with language signals
steps.title: Feed normalized media content into turn orchestration
steps.content: Return normalized transcription or image-derived text/features with source modality and confidence. Preserve original user intent and allow the user to correct a low-confidence transcription or extraction instead of treating model output as ground truth.

connection.label: Text/features + modality confidence
connection.description: Preprocessed content joins the same turn pipeline with provenance and confidence metadata.

steps.phase: Understand each turn and enrich it with language signals
steps.title: Add the language-understanding endpoint
steps.content: The palette has no Azure LUIS/Language endpoint with its service-specific settings. Use the generic custom type to represent the language-understanding boundary. Extract locale, intent, and entities with confidence and model/version metadata; the brief's LUIS hint identifies a role, while the exact currently selected endpoint and migration choice must be confirmed separately.

component.label: Language Understanding — Locale, Intent, Entities
component.description: Multilingual natural-language interpretation behind a replaceable endpoint

properties.subtitle: Locale + intent + entities
properties.purpose: Classify the user's intent and extract entities; return locale, confidence, endpoint/model version, and a safe fallback signal for every supported language.
properties.technology: Azure language-understanding endpoint (LUIS hint; exact service to confirm)
properties.notes: The brief does not enumerate languages or confidence thresholds. Evaluate every approved language and keep unsupported/low-confidence requests on an explicit fallback path.

component.highlightReason: No catalog component exposes the Azure language endpoint; custom-component is the supported generic type and all configured property keys exist in the palette.

steps.phase: Understand each turn and enrich it with language signals
steps.title: Request locale, intent, and entity extraction
steps.content: Send normalized text and the claimed/detected locale to the language endpoint. Preserve the input language and ask for a supported-language result; do not silently translate an unsupported input and count that as successful multilingual support.

connection.label: Text + locale -> intent / entities
connection.description: The orchestrator calls NLU with the original locale and correlated turn ID.

steps.phase: Understand each turn and enrich it with language signals
steps.title: Return structured language signals to orchestration
steps.content: Return the predicted intent, extracted entities, locale, confidence, and endpoint version. The orchestrator applies calibrated routing/fallback policy; a missing entity or low-confidence result should request clarification rather than trigger an unsupported knowledge action.

connection.label: Intent + entities + locale + confidence
connection.description: Structured NLU results inform retrieval, clarification, and response policy.

steps.phase: Understand each turn and enrich it with language signals
steps.title: Add sentiment as a separate conversational signal
steps.content: The palette has no Azure Text Analytics sentiment service. Use the generic custom type for the hinted endpoint. Sentiment can adjust escalation or response tone, but must not overwrite intent, change permissions, or make a high-impact decision without an independently approved policy.

component.label: Sentiment Analysis Endpoint
component.description: Sentiment signal for response tone and escalation policy

properties.subtitle: Text Analytics role
properties.purpose: Return sentiment and confidence as an advisory conversation signal; allow the orchestrator to apply an approved escalation or tone policy without changing the extracted user intent.
properties.technology: Azure Text Analytics sentiment endpoint (exact service to confirm)
properties.notes: Define privacy handling, language coverage, and escalation rules with product owners; sentiment is not a substitute for user intent or a standalone decision.

component.highlightReason: Text Analytics is not a native palette type or monitoring-stack option; custom-component is the supported generic service boundary.

steps.phase: Understand each turn and enrich it with language signals
steps.title: Request sentiment only where the policy needs it
steps.content: The orchestrator can call sentiment analysis on relevant text turns and use the result as a bounded signal. Avoid a mandatory extra dependency on every response if it adds latency without changing user experience; measure its contribution and failure behavior.

connection.label: Relevant text -> sentiment signal
connection.description: Sentiment is invoked where the approved response/escalation policy consumes it.

steps.phase: Understand each turn and enrich it with language signals
steps.title: Return sentiment without conflating it with intent
steps.content: Return sentiment, confidence, language, and model/version metadata to the orchestrator. Keep intent/entity data independently available so analytics can distinguish a user's request from the emotional tone of that request.

connection.label: Sentiment + confidence + locale
connection.description: A separate signal informs the response policy and conversation monitoring.

steps.phase: Understand each turn and enrich it with language signals
steps.title: Choose explicit confidence and clarification behavior
steps.content: A classifier should not force a confident-looking answer when the input is ambiguous. Calibrate intent/entity confidence per supported locale from labeled evaluation data; below the approved threshold, ask a focused clarification or offer a safe handoff. The brief supplies no confidence cutoff, so it must not be invented in this draft.

decision.question: What should happen when intent, entity, transcription, or retrieval confidence is insufficient?
decision.chosen: Use a calibrated, versioned confidence policy to clarify, safely fall back, or hand off; choose thresholds from evaluated data for each supported language.
decision.chosenReason: Explicit uncertainty prevents a weak prediction from becoming a misleading answer and produces an observable recovery path.

alternatives.tradeoff: The highest score can still be unreliable, especially for an unsupported language or noisy media.

alternatives.option: Return a generic error for every ambiguous turn
alternatives.tradeoff: It discards an opportunity to clarify or route the user to a supported channel.

steps.phase: Ground answers, preserve conversation context, and plan scale
steps.title: Add the maintained FAQ knowledge boundary
steps.content: Use the generic custom type for the brief's QnA Maker knowledge-base role because no exact product entry exists in the palette. Keep source ownership, approval, locale, answer version, and refresh workflow here; separate content authoring from the index used for retrieval. Verify the currently selected Azure knowledge service before implementation.

component.label: Approved FAQ Knowledge Base
component.description: Versioned source answers and knowledge ownership

properties.subtitle: QnA Maker role from the brief
properties.purpose: Store approved question/answer content with owner, locale, source, and version; publish changes through review before the search index refreshes.
properties.notes: QnA Maker is the supplied hint, not a validated deployment selection. Confirm the current Azure service, migration path, locale support, and content-retention behavior.

component.highlightReason: No catalog type represents Azure QnA Maker; the generic custom-component is used with supported descriptive fields only.

steps.phase: Ground answers, preserve conversation context, and plan scale
steps.title: Add Azure Cognitive Search as a distinct retrieval service
steps.content: Use the existing Search component with Azure Cognitive Search selected. Configure indexing, locale-aware retrieval, ranking, and source references in the service implementation; the provider selection alone does not define those policies.

component.label: Azure Cognitive Search — FAQ Retrieval
component.description: Locale-aware index and ranked FAQ retrieval with source references

properties.purpose: Index approved FAQ content and return locale-aware ranked matches, source references, and retrieval scores to the orchestrator. Keep the knowledge source of truth separate from its derived search index.

component.highlightReason: The existing Search component now exposes Azure Cognitive Search as a selectable engine.

steps.phase: Ground answers, preserve conversation context, and plan scale
steps.title: Publish approved FAQ changes into the retrieval index
steps.content: Only reviewed knowledge changes flow into the derived index. Record source version and indexing outcome so stale or partially published FAQ content can be diagnosed and rolled back.

connection.label: Reviewed FAQ versions -> locale-aware index
connection.description: The search index is derived from approved, versioned knowledge content.

steps.phase: Ground answers, preserve conversation context, and plan scale
steps.title: Query the index with the understood turn
steps.content: The orchestrator sends the question, locale, intent/entity filters when appropriate, and the minimum needed context to search. Avoid placing full conversation history into every query; use a compact, explicitly governed context representation.

connection.label: Question + locale + approved context
connection.description: Retrieval receives only the signals needed to find relevant approved answers.

steps.phase: Ground answers, preserve conversation context, and plan scale
steps.title: Return ranked evidence rather than an ungrounded answer
steps.content: Return ranked FAQ passages, answer/source IDs, locale, and retrieval confidence. The orchestrator applies a calibrated match policy; when evidence is insufficient, clarify, say the answer is not known, or offer an approved handoff instead of fabricating a fact.

connection.label: Grounded matches + provenance
connection.description: The response policy receives evidence and its source identity for a grounded answer.

steps.phase: Ground answers, preserve conversation context, and plan scale
steps.title: Prefer a grounded FAQ response before open-ended generation
steps.content: The brief calls for conversational AI and knowledge-base answers but does not require free-form generative responses. For this draft, answer from approved FAQ/search evidence, personalize presentation through response templates, and expose citations or source references where the channel allows. If a future product decision adds an LLM, require grounding, refusal behavior, prompt-injection controls, and separate quality evaluation before it can answer unsupported questions.

decision.question: Should every question be answered by unconstrained generative text?
decision.chosen: Use intent-aware, evidence-grounded FAQ answers and channel-aware response templates as the default; treat generative composition as a separately reviewed extension.
decision.chosenReason: This keeps the initial answer path tied to approved knowledge while still allowing customized wording and a future replaceable generation boundary.

alternatives.option: Generate an answer even when retrieval has no strong evidence
alternatives.tradeoff: It may sound fluent while inventing an unsupported answer and undermining the accuracy target.

alternatives.option: Return only a static FAQ string with no response policy
alternatives.tradeoff: It misses channel-specific formatting, clarification, escalation, and safe fallback behavior.

steps.phase: Ground answers, preserve conversation context, and plan scale
steps.title: Add active conversation state for multi-turn behavior
steps.content: Use the existing Cache palette type with Redis as the active conversation-state store. For this draft, enable persistence so active sessions can survive a cache-process restart; confirm the required recovery point, expiry, and privacy behavior before production. Keep only the context needed to resolve references across turns plus turn/version metadata; the brief does not request an indefinite transcript archive.

component.label: Redis Active Conversation State
component.description: Shared low-latency state for continuing multi-turn sessions

properties.purpose: Store compact active-turn context, conversation version, and idempotency metadata for bot instances; minimize sensitive content and apply the approved session expiration and recovery policy.

component.highlightReason: Cache is an exact catalog type with Redis, replication, cluster, persistence, and encryption properties; no unsupported Azure cache type is invented.

steps.phase: Ground answers, preserve conversation context, and plan scale
steps.title: Read and update shared state on every conversation turn
steps.content: The Bot Service reads the current compact context and writes the next version with an idempotent turn identifier. Use an explicit concurrency policy for simultaneous messages in one conversation; a shared Redis cluster avoids pinning a user's multi-turn state to one bot instance.

connection.label: Versioned turn state + idempotency key
connection.description: Shared state supports multi-turn continuity and safe retries across bot instances.

steps.phase: Ground answers, preserve conversation context, and plan scale
steps.title: Choose active context over unbounded conversation history
steps.content: Store compact state required for continuity and resolve retention, deletion, and export separately. Persisting every raw turn in the hot cache increases memory pressure and sensitive-data exposure; retaining no state breaks multi-turn references. If durable transcripts become a product requirement, add an explicitly reviewed storage boundary and retention policy rather than stretching the cache into an archive.

decision.question: What conversation data belongs in the low-latency state store?
decision.chosen: Keep only active, compact context and idempotency/version data in Redis; set expiry and any transcript retention from approved product and privacy policy.
decision.chosenReason: This enables multi-turn continuity without inventing an indefinite transcript-retention requirement or coupling session state to a single bot instance.

alternatives.option: Keep every raw message indefinitely in Redis
alternatives.tradeoff: It creates unbounded memory cost and an unapproved sensitive-data retention policy.
The bot cannot resolve references or honor the explicit multi-turn constraint.

steps.phase: Measure quality, observe conversations, and recover safely
steps.title: Add conversation and service observability
steps.content: Use the existing Monitoring component with Azure Application Insights selected. Capture turn counts, end-to-end and dependency timings, errors, locale, channel, intent, retrieval outcome, sentiment signal, and release/model versions. Avoid logging raw text, images, audio, credentials, or identifiers unless a reviewed privacy policy explicitly permits it.

component.label: Application Insights — Conversation Telemetry
component.description: Correlated turn, dependency, latency, and conversation outcome signals

properties.purpose: Correlate channel turn IDs with gateway, Bot Service, NLU, sentiment, search, and response timings; report errors, locale, retrieval result, and service/model versions without defaulting to raw-content logging. Define redaction, sampling, access, retention, and alert thresholds with the data owner.

component.highlightReason: The existing Monitoring component now exposes Azure Application Insights as a selectable stack.

steps.phase: Measure quality, observe conversations, and recover safely
steps.title: Correlate each bot turn with operational telemetry
steps.content: Emit privacy-filtered turn and dependency events with the same trace ID, including the final channel delivery outcome. This lets operators identify whether latency came from the gateway, preprocessing, NLU, state, retrieval, or response policy and monitor conversations without making raw transcript collection the default.

connection.label: Latency + outcome + redacted turn metadata
connection.description: Bot outcomes and dependency spans are observable under a shared trace identity.

steps.phase: Measure quality, observe conversations, and recover safely
steps.title: Add an explicit labeled-quality evaluation gate
steps.content: The palette has no dedicated service for end-to-end conversational answer evaluation. Use the generic custom type for a versioned evaluation job that checks intent/entities and grounded answer correctness by language and task. Require the measured rate to be strictly above 85%; determine the labeled sample, rubric, confidence treatment, and aggregation with the product owner before the gate can be considered accepted.

component.label: Conversational Quality Evaluation Gate
component.description: Versioned labeled evaluation for NLU and grounded answers by language

properties.subtitle: Strictly above 85% target
properties.purpose: Evaluate labeled intent/entity outcomes and grounded-answer correctness per supported language and task; retain dataset, rubric, endpoint/index version, and error categories for each run.
properties.componentType: Offline AI quality evaluation and promotion gate
properties.notes: The supplied target is accuracy above 85%, not 85% or higher. Confirm the exact metric, labeled examples, language aggregation, confidence policy, and release blocking rule before reporting a pass.

component.highlightReason: No exact evaluation-gate palette entry exists; this custom component uses only the generic type's supported descriptive fields.

steps.phase: Measure quality, observe conversations, and recover safely
steps.title: Use reviewed, privacy-safe outcomes for quality evaluation
steps.content: Feed the evaluation process only approved redacted samples and labels from permitted sources. Do not equate production telemetry or unreviewed thumbs-up feedback with ground truth; keep the evaluation set versioned and prevent leakage between tuning and holdout examples.

connection.label: Permitted outcomes + human-reviewed labels
connection.description: Quality evaluation consumes approved samples and labels, not unrestricted raw conversation logs.

steps.phase: Measure quality, observe conversations, and recover safely
steps.title: Promote only the evaluated response policy and endpoint versions
steps.content: Tie an approved evaluation result to the exact NLU endpoint, knowledge index, response policy, and orchestrator version. Promotion should be blocked when the agreed strict accuracy metric fails or when evaluation evidence is missing; retain the previous known-good configuration for rollback.

connection.label: Approved NLU / index / response-policy versions
connection.description: Only an evaluated, traceable behavior configuration is eligible for activation.

steps.phase: Measure quality, observe conversations, and recover safely
steps.title: Route each language through an evaluated capability
steps.content: The brief requires multiple languages but supplies no language inventory. Detect or receive locale, route only to a language capability that has been evaluated, and expose unsupported-language behavior clearly. Translation can broaden reach but can alter intent/entities and add latency, so make it an explicit, separately evaluated option rather than an invisible fallback.

decision.question: How should multilingual requests be handled when language coverage differs?
decision.chosen: Maintain a confirmed supported-language matrix and route each request to evaluated NLU, sentiment, and retrieval behavior for that locale; disclose and safely handle unsupported locales.
decision.chosenReason: Per-language routing makes both coverage and accuracy measurable while avoiding a false claim that one language model works equally across all locales.

alternatives.option: Translate every request silently into one default language
alternatives.tradeoff: Translation may alter entities or intent, adds another latency dependency, and obscures native-language quality.

alternatives.option: Treat any returned locale as supported
alternatives.tradeoff: Detection alone does not prove intent, sentiment, or knowledge-answer quality in that language.

steps.phase: Measure quality, observe conversations, and recover safely
steps.title: Scale bot capacity from observed conversation pressure
steps.content: The design must support 10k+ concurrent conversations, but the brief gives no per-instance capacity. Load-test with realistic turn duration, channel mix, and media payloads; use the measured saturation point to choose autoscaling thresholds and headroom.

scaleTrigger.metric: Active conversations per bot replica, queue/wait time, saturation, and end-to-end latency by modality
scaleTrigger.action: Scale Bot Service workers horizontally and distribute turns across healthy instances before measured saturation causes the under-two-second target to fail; validate the design at 10k+ concurrent conversations.
scaleTrigger.impact: Adds turn-processing capacity while preserving the shared stateless service boundary and Redis-backed conversation continuity.

steps.phase: Measure quality, observe conversations, and recover safely
steps.title: Scale the shared conversation store from measured pressure
steps.content: Monitor Redis command latency, memory pressure, evictions, replication health, and state-restore behavior while the 10k+ concurrency test runs. Any partitioning or capacity decision must preserve per-conversation ordering and a recovery policy; no cache size or session TTL can be derived from the brief alone.

scaleTrigger.metric: Cache memory pressure, command latency, evictions, replication lag, and concurrent-session load-test results
scaleTrigger.action: Adjust cluster capacity or partitioning based on measured state size and access distribution; remove unnecessary context before increasing retained payloads.
scaleTrigger.impact: Protects multi-turn continuity and keeps shared state from becoming the bottleneck as active conversations grow.

steps.phase: Measure quality, observe conversations, and recover safely
steps.title: Scale language and retrieval dependencies independently
steps.content: Break down dependency latency and throttling by locale, model endpoint, and search query. A single healthy Bot Service tier does not prove the NLU or index can sustain the required concurrency; validate vendor quotas and scaling behavior using measured traffic.

scaleTrigger.metric: Per-locale NLU queue time, dependency latency, throttling/fallback rate, and search saturation
scaleTrigger.action: Scale or partition the saturated language/search dependency independently, tune retrieval, or apply bounded admission control while preserving a safe fallback.
scaleTrigger.impact: Avoids scaling every layer together and directs capacity to the dependency that actually limits the turn.

steps.phase: Measure quality, observe conversations, and recover safely
steps.title: Fail safely when a dependency or answer is uncertain
steps.content: Define timeouts and bounded retries from the approved response-latency budget; retries must not multiply a slow dependency into a longer user wait. If NLU, sentiment, retrieval, or media processing is unavailable, preserve the user's turn and return a clear clarification, known-safe fallback, or supported handoff. Never invent an FAQ answer because search timed out.

decision.question: What does the user receive when a required AI or retrieval dependency is slow or unavailable?
decision.chosen: Use dependency-specific timeouts, bounded/idempotent retries where safe, and a clear fallback or handoff; answer only from approved evidence when the knowledge path is healthy.
decision.chosenReason: This contains dependency failures, protects the latency budget, and makes uncertainty visible rather than returning fabricated content.

alternatives.option: Retry indefinitely until every service responds
alternatives.tradeoff: The response can exceed the latency objective and amplify an outage.

alternatives.option: Return a guessed answer when retrieval fails
alternatives.tradeoff: It converts an infrastructure error into an apparently authoritative but unsupported answer.

steps.phase: Measure quality, observe conversations, and recover safely
steps.title: Review the end-to-end design and unresolved acceptance decisions
steps.content: The applied path is web/mobile or an approved channel adapter -> API Gateway -> Bot Service -> modality normalization when needed -> conversation orchestrator -> language and sentiment signals plus approved FAQ/Cognitive Search evidence -> customized channel response. Redis holds compact shared multi-turn state; privacy-filtered telemetry and a versioned evaluator observe the complete behavior. Before implementation sign-off, confirm channel inventory, language matrix, response-latency clock, accuracy denominator and strict >85% gate, data/retention policy, and measured capacity at 10k+ concurrent conversations. This local review draft makes no claim that the AI quality or live browser-application gates have passed.
